title: Week 1 Tutorials — Photoshop & Premiere Pro Fundamentals
description:
This tutorial set introduces essential post-production workflows for Week 1. Photoshop is used for basic black-and-white conversion and exposure adjustments on still images, while Premiere Pro is used to import, sequence, and export a photo-based video project with attention to rhythm, timing, and minimal sound design.

Adobe Photoshop is a professional image-editing software used to modify, correct, and manipulate still images. In industry contexts, it is widely used for photographic post-production, colour correction, compositing, and preparing images for print, web, and video workflows.

Adobe Premiere Pro is a professional video editing software used to assemble, sequence, and export time-based media. In industry, it is commonly used for film, television, online video, and experimental media production, supporting workflows that combine image, sound, and timing.

description: This tutorial introduces essential Photoshop tools for preparing still images for the Photo Film assignment. You will learn how to open RAW images, convert photographs to black and white, and adjust exposure and contrast using basic tools such as Brightness/Contrast and Levels. The focus is on achieving visual consistency across a sequence rather than stylistic effects. The tutorial also covers how to save edited images correctly for sequencing in Premiere Pro.

description: This tutorial set introduces Adobe Premiere Pro as a tool for assembling still images into a time-based sequence. You will learn how to create a new project, import and organize media, adjust still image duration, sequence photographs on the timeline to shape pacing and rhythm, apply simple transitions (fade in/out and cross overs), add basic titles and credits, and export a 30-second photo film using standard delivery settings.
